body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE TEXT for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in exactly the format asked at the end.

"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG (think Baldur's Gate 3: fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). It is folk horror set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face; drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the stakes are real. Humour is deadpan and sits beside the dread.

THIS SCENE: Chapter 20, "The Roving Rookery". The village of Wickermoor has been swept into a mass hysteria by Golub Graygullet, a pigeon hag who has lived seventy years among the villagers wearing other women's skins, lately as the postmaster Theodora Mayville. She staged a murder, pinned it on the party (four level 10 heroes) with a forged letter, and charmed the whole village: every neighbour is hostile, doors are barred, shops shut, mobs with torches walk the lanes, and grey pigeons line every roof. A tell of the charm is a lilac glint in the eyes. Her flying, walking dovecote stands up on pigeon legs and roams between four roosts. Peeping Albert is her spy: a pudgy pigeon with a wrinkled bald human head, human ears, and hands for talons; he is terrified of dogs. Cast: Constable Doris Squire (tall, stocky, laconic, writes poetry in secret), Deputy Howie Butterman (friendly, false, a hidden cultist), Mayor Wendel Somerton (officious, loves forms, bowler hat, waxed moustache), Tamsin Ledger (deadpan auditor, treats strangeness as a clerical error), Ambrose Quill (grand hopeless poet), Sergeant Gaunt (overconfident coward), Pip Oakum (a small boy who trades buttons), Mrs. Oakum (hill-country twang, a werewolf who only wants to hurt no one), Marianna Grey (shy stablemistress), Weston Murdoch (warm Brightsinger preacher), Hilda Brom (terse huntress), Geneva Fairchild (earnest assistant, lilac eyes), Phillip and Adela Druskenvald (dapper theatrical lord; bright slangy lady), Dani Jenkin (child with a hound called Shuck), Jeremiah Stover (stubborn tuber farmer).

RULES FOR THE TEXT
- Spoken lines: 1 to 3 short sentences, about 12 to 30 words, never over 45. Contractions are normal. People talk in their own voice and do not explain the plot to the audience. Accent is word choice and rhythm, never phonetic spelling.
- Option lines (what the player's party says or does): under 12 words, plain, in the party's voice ("We..." or an imperative).
- Narrator lines ("The Vagrant", a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, never gloating): second person, present tense, one or two sentences, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never the word "suddenly". Never mention the Vagrant by name inside the line.
- No stage directions, asterisks, italics, brackets, placeholders, emoji or em dashes (use commas, periods, colons). Straight quotes only. Do not use the arrow characters -> or => inside the text.
- Content is dark but restrained: no gore, no graphic detail.
- Each brief inside <<...>> says what the line must do; keep its facts, write it as the speaker would say it. Where it says "The Vagrant:" it is a Narrator line.

## The conversation file `hook` (structure is fixed; only the [[n]] markers are yours)

```
# R20 hook: Geneva's plea (route A), Geneva's accusation (route B), and the accusation of the postmaster across her counter (route B, earlier).

~ plea
Narrator: [[1]]
geneva_fairchild [afraid]: [[2]]

-> plea

set rk_started
quest roving_rookery plea

Narrator: [[9]]

Narrator: [[10]]

Narrator: [[18]]

~ accuse_theodora
Narrator: [[19]]

* [Investigation DC 15] [[21]] -> exposed | exposed
* [Intimidation DC 16] [[22]] -> exposed | exposed
* [[23]] -> exposed
* [[24]] -> accuse_wait

~ accuse_wait
theodora_mayville [neutral]: [[25]]
-> END

~ exposed
theodora_mayville [angry]: [[26]]
Narrator: [[27]]
cutscene rk_master_stroke_2
Narrator: [[28]]
cutscene rk_master_stroke_3
Narrator: [[29]]
cutscene end
set golub_exposed
set golub_exposed_early
set geneva_alive
quest roving_rookery exposed
-> END
```

## Briefs

1. node `plea`, narrator: A pale young woman with lilac eyes runs up the north lane, skirts in her fists; the Vagrant, one or two sentences
2. node `plea`, spoken by geneva_fairchild: Geneva, breathless: Theodora is dead on the post office floor, and she is terrified the constable will blame the first strangers she sees. Asks them to look at the body now.
3. node `plea`, option: Ask what happened.
4. node `plea`, option: Say we will come at once.
5. node `plea`, option: Say not yet.
6. node `plea_what`, spoken by geneva_fairchild: Geneva stammers that she found Theodora face down among the letters; nothing was taken, nothing broken, and there is not a mark on her. She will not say more in the street.
7. node `plea_wait`, spoken by geneva_fairchild: Geneva says please do not wait long, she cannot stay alone with it.
8. node `plea_go`, spoken by geneva_fairchild: Geneva, relieved, says to follow her quickly and keep your heads down.
9. node `plea_go`, narrator: The two of you hurry down the lane; the post office door stands open, and inside the lamp has not been lit; one sentence
10. node `geneva_accuses`, narrator: The Vagrant: a posse's torches at the end of the lane, and Geneva stepping out in front of them with the whole village behind her
11. node `geneva_accuses`, spoken by geneva_fairchild: Geneva, her eyes glinting lilac and her voice not her own, accuses the party of plotting to murder Mayor Somerton and of spilling Theodora's secrets; the mob has her letter.
12. node `geneva_accuses`, option: Her eyes have a lilac glint, as if someone were standing behind them.
13. node `geneva_accuses`, option: Insist we never touched the mayor.
14. node `geneva_accuses`, option: Say nothing and look for a way out.
15. node `geneva_charmed`, narrator: The Vagrant: the glint is in her eyes and in every eye behind her, steady as a lantern; this is not anger, it is a hand on a puppet's strings
16. node `geneva_missed`, narrator: The Vagrant: all you can read is a very frightened young woman and a lot of angry neighbours
17. node `geneva_end`, spoken by geneva_fairchild: Geneva, flatly: the constable will hear it; do not run
18. node `geneva_end`, narrator: The Vagrant: pigeons in rows along every roof ridge, all their heads turning to look at you
19. node `accuse_theodora`, narrator: The Vagrant: the postmaster at her counter, gloved left hand flat on a ledger, the pigeon on her shoulder watching you
20. node `accuse_theodora`, spoken by theodora_mayville: Theodora asks pleasantly whether you are here to post something; brisk and kind, with the faintest edge
21. node `accuse_theodora`, option: Lay out the mismatched seals, the changed letters, the glove she never takes off.
22. node `accuse_theodora`, option: Tell her we know what she is and she has one chance to say it.
23. node `accuse_theodora`, option: Name her plainly as the hag who has been reading the valley's mail.
24. node `accuse_theodora`, option: Post a letter, and keep our suspicions.
25. node `accuse_wait`, spoken by theodora_mayville: Theodora stamps the letter and says to come again, in a voice like a closing door
26. node `exposed`, spoken by theodora_mayville: Theodora drops the kindness; she cackles and says the valley will be sorry, and that they were always her pawns
27. node `exposed`, narrator: The Vagrant: the woman sags like a coat off a peg, a smell of feathers fills the room, and out the north window something round is standing up on huge pigeon legs
28. node `exposed`, narrator: The Vagrant: the dovecote, out the north window, rises on huge pigeon legs; the postmaster's skin lies empty on the boards
29. node `exposed`, narrator: The Vagrant: it hops once, twice, and walks off over the roofs toward the moors; the valley will keep this mischief for later

## Reply format
One line per marker, in order, exactly `n => text` (no quotes around the text, no extra lines, no commentary). 29 lines.
result:
1 => A pale girl with lilac eyes comes pelting up the north lane, her skirts bunched tight in her fists. Her breath tears in her throat like dry paper.
2 => Miss Theodora is dead on the post office floor. Please, the constable will blame the first strangers she sees, so you have to come look at her right now.
3 => Tell us what happened.
4 => Lead the way, we will come at once.
5 => We cannot come just yet.
6 => I found her face down among the morning letters. Nothing is taken, nothing is broken, and there is not a mark on her, though I dare not say more in the street.
7 => Please do not be long. I cannot bear to stay in that room alone with her.
8 => Thank heavens. Follow me quickly, and keep your heads down.
9 => You hurry after her down the narrow lane to where the post office door gapes open onto a cold, unlit room.
10 => Pine torches sputter in the damp at the lane's end, and Geneva steps out before the whole massed village.
11 => There they are, the butchers who plotted to murder Mayor Somerton and spilled poor Theodora's secrets! We have your letter in hand, and you will answer for every word!
12 => Study the lilac glint in her eyes, like someone standing behind them.
13 => We never laid a finger on the mayor.
14 => Say nothing and look for a way out.
15 => That lilac glint burns in her eyes and in every pair of eyes behind her, steady as a marsh lantern. This is no honest fury: it is a cold hand working a row of puppets.
16 => For all your squinting through the torchlight, you see only a terrified young woman and a lane full of angry neighbours.
17 => The constable will hear what you have to say. Do not try to run.
18 => High along every wet roof ridge, rows of grey pigeons pivot their heads as one to fix you with their bead-black eyes.
19 => Theodora stands trim behind her counter with her gloved left hand flat on the open ledger, while the fat pigeon on her shoulder watches you without blinking.
20 => Good evening to you, travellers. Have you a parcel for the post, or only a letter that wants a clean seal?
21 => Lay out the mismatched seals, the altered letters, and her unremoved glove.
22 => We know what you are, and you have one chance to confess.
23 => You are the hag who has been reading this valley's mail.
24 => Post a letter and keep our suspicions to ourselves.
25 => There you are, stamped and sorted. Do come again when you have news worth sending.
26 => Oh, clever little strays, poking your noses into my pigeonholes! This whole valley was mine to pluck, and it will weep feathers before I am done with it!
27 => The postmaster sags behind the counter like an old coat slipped off a peg, a thick reek of wet feathers fills the room, and outside the north window something round heaves up on scaly pigeon legs.
28 => Beyond the glass, the great dovecote rises on legs as thick as birch trunks, while Theodora's empty skin lies crumpled on the floorboards.
29 => The rookery hops once, twice, and stalks away across the groaning roofs toward the dark moors, leaving its mischief behind for the valley to keep.
